langchain.title: LangChain (mental model)
langchain.description: Chains, tools, and runnable composition — glue for LLM apps, not a model provider.

steps.heading: LCEL-style chain
steps.caption: Runnable pipeline — input flows through prompt → model → output parser as composable steps.

steps.heading: retrieve | prompt | model
steps.caption: Retrieval chain — retriever augments the prompt before the model call (classic RAG wiring).

steps.heading: Agent executor
steps.caption: Agents in LangChain — tool catalogue + agent executor loop. Same Plan/Act/Observe idea with library helpers.

steps.heading: What LangChain is / is not
steps.caption: Use it for speed of composition; still own prompts, evals, and production concerns yourself.

langgraph.title: LangGraph
langgraph.description: Explicit graphs of nodes and edges with durable state — cycles, branches, and checkpoints.

steps.heading: Simple graph
steps.caption: Graph — nodes are functions on state; edges declare control flow including loops.

steps.heading: State transitions
steps.caption: Shared state — each node reads/writes typed fields instead of burying everything in chat messages.

steps.heading: Durable execution
steps.caption: Checkpoint — after each node, persist state so you can pause for a human or resume after failure.

steps.heading: Fit
steps.caption: Why not a linear chain — when you need cycles, branching, and durable pause, a graph is the honest model.

llamaindex.title: LlamaIndex
llamaindex.description: Data framework centred on indexes, retrievers, and query engines over your documents.

steps.heading: Index build
steps.caption: Ingest — load files, parse into nodes (chunks), attach metadata.

steps.heading: Online query
steps.caption: Query engine — retrieves nodes and synthesises an answer with a chosen response mode.

steps.heading: Index choice (simplified)
steps.caption: Index types — vector, keyword, knowledge graph, etc. Choose based on query patterns.

steps.heading: Sweet spot
steps.caption: Positioning — strongest when your product is document Q&A / RAG; pair with other libs for complex multi-agent ops.

crewai.title: CrewAI
crewai.description: Role-playing crews — agents with jobs, tools, and a process that coordinates tasks.

steps.heading: Crew members
steps.caption: Define agents — each has a role, goal, backstory, and optional tools.

steps.heading: Sequential process
steps.caption: Tasks — describe expected output; assign to an agent; chain via context from prior tasks.

steps.heading: Hierarchical
steps.caption: Hierarchical process — a manager agent delegates and reviews, similar to a supervisor pattern.

steps.heading: Illustrative call counts
steps.caption: Watch coordination cost — crews multiply calls. Measure quality vs a single agent baseline.

autogen.title: AutoGen
autogen.description: Conversational multi-agent patterns — agents messaging each other under group-chat rules.

steps.heading: Assistant ↔ UserProxy
steps.caption: Two-agent chat — assistant proposes; user proxy may execute code or tools and return results.

steps.heading: Speaker selection
steps.caption: Group chat — a manager selects the next speaker based on messages and roles.

steps.heading: Without vs with max_rounds
steps.caption: Termination — max rounds, explicit TERMINATE, or human stop. Without this, chats thrash.

steps.heading: Takeaway
steps.caption: Fit — excellent for research-style collaborative chats; production systems often move to explicit graphs later.

google-adk.title: Google ADK (conceptual)
google-adk.description: Agent Development Kit patterns — structured agents, tools, and runners aimed at Google’s ecosystem.

steps.heading: Agent spec
steps.caption: Agent definition — instructions + tools + optional sub-agents as a declarative unit.

steps.heading: Execution
steps.caption: Runner — executes the agent loop, manages session state, and applies callbacks/hooks.

steps.heading: Sub-agent call
steps.caption: Delegation — parent agent routes to a sub-agent with a narrower tool set (supervisor-like).

steps.heading: Practical advice
steps.caption: Portability — kits speed integration with a cloud; keep business logic and policies cloud-agnostic where you can.

litellm.title: LiteLLM
litellm.description: One OpenAI-compatible interface over many providers — routing, fallbacks, and spend tracking.

steps.heading: N SDKs
steps.caption: Without a router — every provider SDK is a separate code path and failure mode.

steps.heading: Unified call
steps.caption: With LiteLLM — one client shape; model string selects the backend.

steps.heading: Fallback chain
steps.caption: Fallbacks — if primary 429s/5xx, try the next model in the list. Latency rises; availability rises.

steps.heading: Common knobs
steps.caption: Ops features — budgets, logging callbacks, virtual keys. Still verify provider-specific limits yourself.

framework-comparison.title: Framework comparison
framework-comparison.description: Choose by primary abstraction: chains, graphs, indexes, crews, or provider routers.

steps.heading: Job → abstraction
steps.caption: Map problems to abstractions — start from the job, not the GitHub stars.

steps.heading: Center of gravity
steps.caption: Overlap is real — LangChain can do RAG; LlamaIndex can do agents. Prefer the library whose defaults match your center of gravity.

steps.heading: Portability effort (illustrative)
steps.caption: Cost of switching — prompts and evals should be portable; deep framework lock-in should not hold your policies.

steps.heading: Sane path
steps.caption: Decision rule — prototype in the friendliest fit, productionise with clear state, guardrails, and evals regardless of brand.
